Dataset Name: sub-0_ses-1_events.tsv
Dataset Description: LibriBrain Events - Session 1

A time-aligned, hierarchical transcription of spoken audio. Each row represents either a word-level or phoneme-level alignment segment (or silence), extracted from continuous audio and annotated with timing metadata across multiple time bases (e.g., chapter, sentence, and absolute time). 

Columns:
- **idx** — Sequential index of the segment.
- **wavile** — Relative filesystem path to the audio or segment directory.
- **kind** — Type of segment: `silence`, `word`, or `phoneme`.
- **segment** — The surface form of the segment (e.g., word string or phoneme label). `silence` rows may be empty.
- **sentenceidx** — Index of the sentence within the chapter to which this segment belongs.
- **wordidx** — Index of the word within the sentence (present for word and phoneme segments).
- **phonemeidx** — Index of the phoneme within the word (only for phoneme rows).
- **timemeg** — Time in seconds relative to the synchronized MEG/EEG recording timeline.
- **timeds** — Time in seconds relative to the corresponding aligned text/audio dataset.
- **timechapter** — Time in seconds relative to the beginning of the chapter.
- **timesentence** — Time in seconds relative to the beginning of the sentence.
- **duration** — Duration of the segment in seconds.

PREVIOUS EXPLORATION:

Hypothesis: Brain activity in the 30–50 Hz gamma band preceding a phoneme onset can predict the duration of that phoneme.

Experiment objective: Build a regression model predicting phoneme duration from pre‐onset gamma‐band MEG power.

Steps for the programmer:
1. For each session, load MEG and phoneme events with timemeg and duration.  2. Epoch MEG data (–0.2 to 0 s) before phoneme onset.  3. Bandpass filter epochs in 30–50 Hz.  4. Compute average power across the entire pre‐onset window for each channel and epoch.  5. Construct feature vector per epoch: average power from a subset of channels or principal components of channel‐wise features.  6. Fit a regularized linear regression (e.g., RidgeCV) to predict phoneme duration using pre‐onset features, using cross‐validation within each session.  7. Evaluate model performance (R², RMSE) and test whether prediction accuracy is significantly above chance via permutation testing.

Deliverables:
1. Regression model coefficients or component weights.  2. Prediction performance metrics with confidence intervals.  3. Permutation‐test p‐value showing significance of prediction.

Analysis:
The regression pipeline ran successfully for all 10 sessions (each with ~20 phoneme epochs).  Key results:
- R² was near zero or negative for every session (−0.005 to −0.000), RMSE ~0.056–0.074 s.
- Regularization picked the largest alpha (1000) in every session, indicating heavy shrinkage.
- Permutation p-values were not significant in 9/10 sessions (all p > 0.1), with one marginal p = 0.02 in Session 2 despite R²≈0.
- PCA captured 20–90% variance in the first few components, but downstream prediction remained poor.

Overall, pre-onset 30–50 Hz power did not predict phoneme duration above chance under this pipeline.

Review:
Hypothesis: Pre‐onset gamma‐band (30–50 Hz) MEG power can predict phoneme duration.

Results:
• Data: ~20 phoneme epochs per session, features = average 30–50 Hz power over −0.2–0 s across 306 channels reduced via PCA to ≤20 components.
• Model: Ridge regression (α selected via nested CV), evaluated with 5‐fold CV and 100 permutations per session.
• Performance: R² ≈ −0.005 to 0.0, RMSE ≈ 0.056–0.074 s. Regularization was maximal (α=1000) each session, indicating no predictive signal. Permutation test p-values >0.1 in 9/10 sessions (one marginal at p=0.02 despite R²≈0).

Findings: Pre‐onset gamma‐band power does not predict phoneme duration above chance in any session under this pipeline.

PREVIOUS EXPLORATION:

Hypothesis: Channels over the left auditory cortex exhibit stronger gamma‐band increases after phoneme onset than right‐hemisphere homologues, reflecting left‐lateralized phoneme processing.

Experiment objective: Compare post‐onset gamma‐band (30–50 Hz) power changes between left and right auditory ROI channels.

Steps for the programmer:
1. Parse `channel_names` to identify left vs. right temporal channels (e.g., channels with ‘LT’ vs. ‘RT’ in names). 2. For each session and each phoneme event, epoch 0–0.2 s post‐onset and bandpass filter in 30–50 Hz. 3. Compute mean power change relative to a pre‐onset baseline (–0.2 to 0 s) for each channel and epoch. 4. For each epoch, average the percent‐change power over left ROI and right ROI separately. 5. Across all epochs in a session, perform a paired t‐test comparing left vs. right ROI power changes. 6. Aggregate results across sessions and test consistency with a one‐sample t‐test on left–right differences.

Deliverables:
1. Session‐wise t‐statistic and p‐value for left vs. right gamma increase. 2. Grand‐mean and SEM of left–right power difference. 3. ROI channel lists and topographies.

Analysis:
The ROI‐based gamma‐band comparison ran successfully across all 10 sessions. Session‐wise paired t‐tests (left vs. right post‐onset percent‐change) yielded:
• Session 1: n=9592, t=2.641, p=0.008
• Session 2: n=12646, t=3.474, p=0.001
• Session 3: n=12801, t=1.336, p=0.182

• Session 9: n=8808,  t=0.354, p=0.724
• Session 10: n=6075, t=−0.700, p=0.484

Across sessions (one‐sample t‐test on left–right differences): mean_diff=0.677 %, SEM=0.300 %, t=2.256, p=0.050.

ROI channels identified:
Left: MEG0111–MEG0443 (48 channels covering codes 11–49)
Right: MEG2311–MEG2643 (48 channels covering codes 231–269)

Review:
The analysis was implemented faithfully according to the plan. ROI channels were correctly identified using sensor numbering, epochs were extracted, power computed, percent-change calculated, and paired t-tests performed per session, followed by a group-level test. The deliverables are met: session-wise t-statistics and p-values; grand-mean and SEM; ROI channel lists. The findings show significant left>right gamma increase in sessions 1,2,7, and marginal effect across sessions (p=0.050).

Hypothesis: The magnitude of beta‐band (15–25 Hz) rebound following phoneme onset is greater when the phoneme occurs in early sentences of a chapter compared to late sentences.

Experiment objective: Test sentence position effects on post‐onset beta rebound.

Steps for the programmer:
1. Load phoneme events and extract timechapter and timesentence for grouping. 2. Define early‐sentence phonemes (timesentence <= median) vs. late‐sentence. 3. For each session, epoch −0.2 to 0.8 s around timemeg for each group. 4. Bandpass filter epochs in 15–25 Hz; compute analytic amplitude via Hilbert transform. 5. For each epoch, compute baseline‐normalized amplitude time course; measure rebound as mean amplitude in 0.3–0.6 s post‐onset minus mean in −0.2–0 s. 6. Compare rebound between early vs. late sentences with paired t‐tests per session and group‐level one‐sample t‐test on differences.

Deliverables:
1. Rebound magnitudes per group. 2. Session‐wise t‐tests and group‐level result. 3. Time‐course plots of beta amplitude.

{"code":"import numpy as np
import h5py
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.signal import butter, sosfiltfilt, hilbert
from scipy.stats import ttest_ind, ttest_1samp

# Parameters
meg_files = [f"sub-0_ses-{i}_meg.h5" for i in range(1, 11)]
event_files = [f"sub-0_ses-{i}_events.tsv" for i in range(1, 11)]
band = (15, 25)  # beta band
baseline_win = (-0.2, 0.0)
rebound_win = (0.3, 0.6)
epoch_win = (-0.2, 0.8)

# Accumulators for group time-course
epoch_len = None
global_sum_tc_early = None
global_sum_tc_late = None
global_count_early = 0
global_count_late = 0
session_results = []

for meg_f, evt_f in zip(meg_files, event_files):
    # Load MEG data
    with h5py.File(meg_f, 'r') as f:
        data = f['data'][:]      # (306, n_samples)
        times = f['times'][:]    # (n_samples,)
        sf = f.attrs.get('sample_frequency', 250.0)
    n_samples = len(times)

    # Continuous average across channels
    avg_signal = data.mean(axis=0)
    # Design filter
    sos = butter(4, band, btype='band', fs=sf, output='sos')
    # Filter and analytic amplitude
    filtered = sosfiltfilt(sos, avg_signal)
    amp_env = np.abs(hilbert(filtered))

    # Load events, select phonemes
    df = pd.read_csv(evt_f, sep='\t')
    df = df[df['kind'] == 'phoneme'].copy()
    if df.empty:
        continue
    # Group by early vs late
    med = df['timesentence'].median()
    early_df = df[df['timesentence'] <= med]
    late_df = df[df['timesentence'] > med]

    # Epoch parameters
    pre_samples = int(round(-epoch_win[0] * sf))  # 0.2 * sf
    post_samples = int(round(epoch_win[1] * sf))  # 0.8 * sf
    curr_epoch_len = pre_samples + post_samples
    if epoch_len is None:
        epoch_len = curr_epoch_len
        global_sum_tc_early = np.zeros(epoch_len)
        global_sum_tc_late = np.zeros(epoch_len)
    # Per-session accumulators
    sum_tc_early = np.zeros(epoch_len)
    sum_tc_late = np.zeros(epoch_len)
    reb_early = []
    reb_late = []

    # Helper to process a set
    def process_events(evt_times, reb_list, sum_tc, count_holder):
        count = 0
        for t0 in evt_times:
            idx = np.searchsorted(times, t0)
            start = idx - pre_samples
            end = idx + post_samples
            if start < 0 or end > n_samples:
                continue
            epoch = amp_env[start:end]
            if len(epoch) != epoch_len:
                continue
            # baseline and rebound indices
            t = np.linspace(epoch_win[0], epoch_win[1], epoch_len, endpoint=False)
            base_idx = (t >= baseline_win[0]) & (t < baseline_win[1])
            reb_idx = (t >= rebound_win[0]) & (t < rebound_win[1])
            base_mean = epoch[base_idx].mean()
            reb_mean = epoch[reb_idx].mean()
            reb_list.append(reb_mean - base_mean)
            sum_tc += epoch
            count += 1
        return count

    # Process early and late events
    n_early = process_events(early_df['timemeg'], reb_early, sum_tc_early, None)
    n_late = process_events(late_df['timemeg'], reb_late, sum_tc_late, None)

    # Session statistics
    if n_early == 0 or n_late == 0:
        continue
    mean_early = np.mean(reb_early)
    mean_late = np.mean(reb_late)
    # Independent t-test
    t_stat, p_val = ttest_ind(reb_early, reb_late, equal_var=False)
    session_results.append({
        'session': meg_f,
        'mean_early': mean_early,
        'mean_late': mean_late,
        't_stat': t_stat,
        'p_val': p_val,
        'n_early': n_early,
        'n_late': n_late
    })
    # Accumulate global time-course
    global_sum_tc_early += sum_tc_early
    global_sum_tc_late += sum_tc_late
    global_count_early += n_early
    global_count_late += n_late

# Print session-wise results
print("=== Session-wise Beta Rebound Comparison ===")
diffs = []
for res in session_results:
    diff = res['mean_early'] - res['mean_late']
    diffs.append(diff)
    print(f"{res['session']}: n_early={res['n_early']}, n_late={res['n_late']}, "
          f"mean_early={res['mean_early']:.4f}, mean_late={res['mean_late']:.4f}, "
          f"t={res['t_stat']:.3f}, p={res['p_val']:.3f}")

# Group-level one-sample t-test on differences
diffs = np.array(diffs)
group_t, group_p = ttest_1samp(diffs, 0)
mean_diff = diffs.mean()
sem_diff = diffs.std(ddof=1) / np.sqrt(len(diffs))
print("\n=== Group-level one-sample t-test (early - late) ===")
print(f"mean_diff={mean_diff:.4f}, SEM={sem_diff:.4f}, t={group_t:.3f}, p={group_p:.3f}")

# Time-course plot
time_vec = np.linspace(epoch_win[0], epoch_win[1], epoch_len, endpoint=False)
global_mean_tc_early = global_sum_tc_early / global_count_early
global_mean_tc_late = global_sum_tc_late / global_count_late
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 4))
plt.plot(time_vec, global_mean_tc_early, label='Early sentences')
plt.plot(time_vec, global_mean_tc_late, label='Late sentences')
plt.axvline(0, color='k', linestyle='--')
plt.xlabel('Time (s) relative to phoneme onset')
plt.ylabel('Beta amplitude (15–25 Hz)')
plt.title('Beta rebound: Early vs Late sentences')
plt.legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()"}
